AlikeRange.description:
Two angles a family's flats measure alike at: the family's own angle
term, from pairs of its sessions compared directly. A flat at one end
serves the family's lights at the other (see [`AlikeRange::serves`]),
from the light's side of every change.

arcs.description:
The arc each alike pair it rests on spans, going round from `low`
to `high`, never more than a half turn.

ends.description:
The recorded angles of the sessions at each end, the short way
round from the first to the second.

groups.description:
The family's groups its pairs come from, and the carrying class
they share ([`Family::carry_class`]): it serves flats of the groups
of that class only.

nights.description: Flat nights the pairs reach, both ends together.

sessions.description: Distinct sessions and flat nights at each end.

span.description: The span from the first end to the second.

AlikeRangeNote.description: A family's [`model::AlikeRange`] as a light's account names it.

carried.description:
Its pairs were all measured in other groups of the family than the
flats', across camera-side dust changes only.

flatsAngle.description: The angle of the flats the light's master is built from.

label.description: "101.9–102.2° and 104.2°": the angles at its two ends.

AngleSpan.description:
The recorded angles of one rotation cluster of a family, lowest to
highest going round the circle from `low`.

AngleTerm.description:
How much a rig's flats depend on the rotator angle: same-filter sessions
at different angles shot within one flat session window.

Answer.description: The operation's native return value, before C property-name translation.

Application.description: How a session's flat applies, once its masters are built.

pedestal.description:
The pedestal subtracted before the flat, in ADU, for
[`FlatUse::FittedPedestal`].

pedestalHint.description: The pedestal the camera's recorded offset predicts: [`pedestal_hint`].

sampleLights.description:
The lights to fit the pedestal from, for
[`FlatUse::NeedsPedestalFit`]: [`pedestal_sample_lights`].

oneOf.description: Each light's frames chosen by time, cohort and validity.
Every compatible frame of the kind taken whole, as one supplied set.

Boundary.description: Why two neighbouring groups stay apart.

before.description:
The last session before and the first after, as indices into the
book's sessions.

byHand.description:
Set when a person's choice, not the measurements, put it here: a
split where the nights measure alike, or a split the measurements
make that a person joined (then it lies inside a group).

drift.description:
When the neighbours themselves are alike but the groups are not: the
worst pair across the boundary, by session index, and its distance.

dust.description:
The neighbouring pair's metrics, fractions of the background; absent
when that pair was not compared.

opens.description: The first session of the later group: where the edge's window ends.

start.description: The last flat before and the first flat after, Unix seconds.

vignetting.description:
The neighbouring pair's deepest change of vignetting, and the
changes.

CalibrationFrame.description:
One catalog row: a raw calibration frame, or a master another program
integrated.

darkSubtracted.description:
A master whose dark signal was removed before it was integrated, as
its `DARKSUB` header records, or a host that adopts it treats it.
Only such a flat master may serve lights at another gain and offset
([`rules::Rules::admits_sensor`]).

isMaster.description:
An integrated master from other software rather than a raw frame.
Matched leniently (its producer strips most settings) and used as a
master as-is instead of being integrated.

keptOut.description:
Why this frame stays out of masters and exports: a person kept it
out ("by hand"), or its grade is poor and this is the main finding.
A frame not graded yet keeps the stray-light mark of the older dark
check. Absent when the frame serves.

readoutModeName.description:
The readout mode's name when the header spelled it that way, matched
independently of its numeric index.

rotation.description: Rotator angle in degrees at capture, when the rig recorded one.

sourceVerified.description:
Set after the current file (or a basename-remapped file) has been
checked against this catalog row's hard settings.

validDirection.description: User-set validity boundary; absent means both directions.

ChangeOption.description: A measured optical change to which a personal side choice can refer.

key.description: Stable native event or evidence identity.

Choice.description: A quality override tied to the exact reviewed source.

choice.description: A user quality decision; physical gates still apply.

fingerprint.description: Metadata identity captured when this file was inspected.

ChoiceNote.description: A person's choice for a light, as its account shows it.

changeKey.description: The change it is about, as recorded; none for a group.

label.description: What it was about, in words.

orphaned.description:
Why it does not apply, when it finds nothing to apply to. It stays
recorded until a person resets it.

ComparisonRow.description: Two sessions' metrics as the catalog keeps them.

vignetting.description:
The deepest change of vignetting, a fraction of the background: a
shadow from the border that moved or deepened, such as a guider's
prism turned with the camera. The flats differ, so it parts groups
as dust does, but it is not dust.

DarkMeasurement.description:
What [`measure_dark`] found in one bias or dark frame. Values are in the
frame's own sample units.

columnBanding.description: Robust spread of column means once a slow trend is removed.

hotThreshold.description: The level plus [`DarkMeasureOptions::hot_sigma`] times the noise.

level.description:
Median of every sixteenth sample: the estimator
`seiza_stacking::DarkLevel` uses.

noise.description:
Pixel-scale noise from second differences, along whichever axis is
quieter so banding does not inflate it. Outliers are clipped, and the
rest give a root mean square, which moves smoothly even on integer
samples.

rowBanding.description: Robust spread of row means once a slow trend is removed.

sigma.description:
Normal-equivalent median absolute deviation of those samples around
the level. It includes glow and pattern as well as noise.

DustFeature.description:
One dust shadow. Positions and sizes are in sensor pixels.

Construct with [`Default::default`] and set what is known; more fields may
be added without a major version.

depth.description:
How much light it takes, as a fraction of the response around it:
0.1 means a tenth less light. A compact dip's deepest point; a disk's
or donut's ring, never its bright centre.

distanceMm.description:
How far in front of the sensor the dust sits, in millimetres, from
the shadow's diameter and the [`Optics`]; only for disks and donuts
measured with optics.

hole.description:
A donut's hole: the radius of its bright centre as a fraction of
[`Self::radius`].

radius.description:
Radius: a disk's or donut's rim; for a compact dip, that of a disc of
the same area. 0 in measurements made before shapes were reported.

seenIn.description:
In how many of a session's flats it shows, where it was found on the
session's stack ([`find_session_dust`]). Dust holds still across
flats shot a minute apart; noise does not.

x.description:
Centre column: the centroid of a compact dip, the rim's centre of a
disk or donut.

DustShape.description: What a dust feature looks like.

oneOf.description: A small dip, a few pixels to a few dozen across.

A small dip that is not round: elongated or ragged, as dust on the
window often is.
A filled out-of-focus disk.
An out-of-focus ring around a central obstruction's bright shadow.

A large shadow that is not one circle: overlapping out-of-focus
shadows, each with a rim, that do not separate. Its radius is that of
a disc of the same area.

Edge.description: Which part of the border a vignetting shadow hangs from.

oneOf.description: Which frames a light's masters take: stacks build new masters.

What the light checks flag. Nothing is rebuilt; the checks run again
on the headers they kept.

How calibration frames are graded. Grading runs again on the stored
measurements; a frame that turns poor leaves its masters.

Epoch.description: One run of lights of a rig with one sky − mechanical offset.

offset.description: Sky − mechanical, degrees, modulo a half turn (see [`half`]).

EpochSample.description: A rig's sky-minus-mechanical angle, modulo a half turn, at a Unix time.

Event.description:
A rig-wide change: boundaries of one rig that overlap in time and share
a spot.

byHand.description:
Made only of splits a person made where the flats measure alike:
the person's word, not a measured change.

cameraSide.description:
Seen in two filters, or in two response families of one filter: on
the camera side, so it applies to every filter of the rig.

families.description: The response families it was seen in, by index.

rotations.description: The angle of each response family it was seen in.

spots.description: The spots of the member with the most dust.

start.description: The narrowest window any member gives.

vignetting.description:
The deepest change of vignetting among the members, and that
member's changes.

withinFlatRun.description:
The window is shorter than one flat run ([`FLAT_RUN_SECONDS`]): the
change landed between the flats of one twilight, or its members
are two changes that met there.

EventNote.description: A change as a light's account names it.

byHand.description:
A split a person made where the flats measure alike, not a
measured change.

start.description: The window it happened in, Unix seconds.

EventPlacement.description:
An automatic event placement and the response pair from which a correction
map can be measured. Personal choices are returned separately on the light.

EvidenceFit.description: One filter's fit within an imaging session.

carried.description: How much of the change the lights carry: 0 none, 1 all of it.

spread.description:
Spread of that estimate over placebo positions; none when too few
placebos fit in the frame.

Family.description: A family of sessions: one rig, filter, sensor mode and rotation cluster.

alikeRanges.description:
The angles its flats measure alike at ([`AlikeRange`]), by their
first end. Empty unless enough pairs measured alike.

angles.description:
The recorded angles of each rotation cluster it joins, in angle
order: its measured angle range. Empty for flats that record none.

boundaries.description: Indices into the book's boundaries, between consecutive groups.

carryClass.description:
Per group, the class of groups an alike range carries across: the
next group shares its class only when the change between them is
camera-side dust ([`Book::carries_angle_term`]).

familyKey.description:
The sessions' family key: rig, filter, optics and sensor mode,
rotation aside.

groups.description: Session indices per group, in time order.

joined.description:
Measured splits a person joined, inside a group now: indices into
the book's boundaries, in time order.

rotation.description:
The middle angle of its largest rotation cluster; absent for flats
that record none.

FamilyBasis.description: How a light's response family was chosen.

oneOf.description: The only candidate, at the light's recorded angle.

Its imaging session's own lights follow this family's flats. `moved`
when that is not the family at its recorded angle; a move stands
only when `corroborated` says what else points there.

Two or more candidates, and its lights could not tell them apart
(`undecided`) or have not been read: the family at its recorded
angle stands.

Its lights point to another family (`pointed`) than the one at its
recorded angle, and nothing confirms it: it keeps the flats at its
recorded angle and is flagged.
A person chose one of its groups for the light.

FamilyChoice.description: The response family a light's flats come from.

atRecorded.description: Whether the family has flats at the light's recorded angle.

shift.description:
How far the light's angle turns into the chosen family's nearest
session's epoch: 0 when nothing re-homed.

FamilyEvidenceRow.description:
What some of an imaging session's lights said about which response
family their flats come from: the lights of one filter, one target and
one recorded angle (lights within the rig's rotation tolerance of each
other), so a background never mixes two fields or two angles.

angle.description: The lights' middle recorded angle, and the lowest and highest.

chosen.description: The family the lights follow, when one stood clear.

key.description:
The candidates, the sessions standing for them, which of those
measured alike, and the choice algorithm, digested
(`Book::family_evidence_key`): a row whose key is not the current
one is not read.

pairs.description: Each pair of candidates, as the lights' background fitted it.

start.description: The first and last of the lights, Unix seconds.

FamilyPairRow.description: One pair of candidate families against a session's background.

carried.description:
0 follows `first`, 1 follows `second`; absent when nothing compact
tells the two apart.

outcome.description:
`alike` (nothing compact tells them apart), `unfitted` (the
background could not be weighed against them) or `fit`.

FamilyProbe.description:
Inputs for a host's response-choice pixel pass. Candidate and representative
indices refer to this snapshot. Reuse `key` on the resulting family evidence
row; changes to the candidates or their measurements invalidate old evidence.

FieldKind.description: What kind of value a setting holds, with its range.

zero.description: What zero means, when it means something other than zero.

oneOf.description:
A light check's mode. `levels` are the levels it raises on its own,
so a check that only ever says "check" offers no advisory step.

FileCalibrationSession.description:
One file-backed calibration recipe and its complete light-matching gate.
The rotation basis is part of `tolerances`; no previous session's settings
are inherited. Paths name already-built masters, not raw master inputs.

normalizedFullScale.description:
Convert only a declared 0:1 source range to this full scale, as PSF
Guard's image loader does with 65535 ADU. None preserves stored units.

pedestal.description:
PSF Guard's fitted-pedestal fallback: a calibrated/normalized flat
plus a synthetic constant bias applied to the lights. Requires no
bias or dark file. The host retains the fit's evidence in its recipe.

FileStamp.description: A file's size and modification time, in nanoseconds since 1970.

Finding.description: One measurement that crossed a limit, with the numbers behind it.

value.description: The measured value, in the unit [`Self::code`] names.

FindingCode.description:
What a finding measured. The name is stable and machine-readable; each
variant says what [`Finding::value`] holds.

oneOf.description: Flat: share of samples at full scale.
Flat: median of the brightest channel as a share of full scale.
Flat: median of the dimmest channel as a share of full scale.

Flat: largest difference between this frame's illumination pattern
and the set's, as a fraction of the response.
Flat: compact dips in this frame, steady or not.

Flat: compact dips in this frame that do not hold steady across the
set.

Flat set: changing dips present in more than half the frames, which a
median-based master keeps.

Bias: distance of this frame's level from the set median, in units of
the set's median pixel noise.

Dark: how far this frame's level sits above the quietest frame's, in
units of that frame's robust pixel spread. Light reaching the sensor
lifts the level.
Bias or dark: pixel noise as a ratio to the set median.
Bias or dark: spread of row levels as a ratio to the pixel noise.
Bias or dark: spread of column levels as a ratio to the pixel noise.
Dark: hot pixel count as a ratio to the set median.

Fit.description:
A background weighed against one change: how much of it the background
carries, how sure that is, and the side that says.

carried.description: How much of the change the lights carry: 0 none, 1 all of it.

spread.description:
Spread of that estimate over placebo positions; infinite when no
shadow had room for enough placebos (written as `null`).

verdict.description: The side the fit decides for, or undecided.

FlatAttempt.description:
One flat master build, as its judgement needs it: the frames the
integrator combined and how far each disagreed with the master.

disagreement.description:
For each of `used`, the master's feature pixels it disagrees at;
empty when the stability was not measured.

driftThreshold.description:
The disagreement at which a frame drifts: it was looking through a
different sensor window.

featurePixels.description: The master's feature pixels the frames were compared at.

label.description:
What a note calls the set; "20 G flats from 2026-09-10" when absent.
Never affects the decision.

memo.description:
A remembered judgement of a set once found unstable: its record
remains, its file does not, so it never serves as it is.

used.description: The frames combined, by UUID, in the order they were offered.

FlatBasis.description: Why a light's flats are the ones they are.

oneOf.description: No measured change touches the light: the nearest flats, as always.
Flats from the light's own side of each change near it.

leftOut.description: Matching flats left out for being on the other side.

oneOf.description:
None at its angle on its side; flats from the nearest other angle on
its side, which this rig's measurements allow.

rotationToleranceDeg.description:
The rotation tolerance the stacker must hold this light to so
those flats pass: the angle between them and the light, plus the
rig's own tolerance. Absent when either angle is unknown.

oneOf.description:
None on its side at any allowed angle; flats at its angle from the
other side, carried across by the change's map.

Its flats are all from the other side of a change, and nothing can
stand in.
Shot while a change happened; nothing tells which side it is on.

then.description:
What another change it does stand clear of chose, such as
another angle's flats or a correction: its flats and gate are
that one's, and the light keeps its Check for this one.

oneOf.description: A person chose the group its flats come from, over every change.

FlatCorrection.description:
The correction a light's flat master takes: the flats at its angle,
from the other side of a change, carried across it by the change's map.

beforeResponse.description: The before and after sessions the map is measured from.

key.description: Key of the correction, for master and stack identities.

lightSide.description:
The side the light is on: `before` divides the flats by the map,
`after` multiplies.

FlatCorrectionPlan2.description: A native correction with exact response dependencies and affected lights.

divide.description: Whether the full change map divides the source flat.

lightIndices.description: Affected indices in the original light order.

FlatFamily.description:
The response family a light's flats come from, when grouping measured
it: which family, how it was chosen, and the gate a stack holds the
light to for it.

oneOf.description: The only candidate, at the light's recorded angle.

Its imaging session's own lights follow this family's flats. `moved`
when that is not the family at its recorded angle; a move stands
only when `corroborated` says what else points there.

Two or more candidates, and its lights could not tell them apart
(`undecided`) or have not been read: the family at its recorded
angle stands.

Its lights point to another family (`pointed`) than the one at its
recorded angle, and nothing confirms it: it keeps the flats at its
recorded angle and is flagged.
A person chose one of its groups for the light.

alikeRange.description:
When those flats lie at another angle inside a span the family's
flats measure alike across: the span and its evidence.

atRecorded.description: Whether the family has flats at the light's recorded angle.

candidates.description: The candidates within the angle prior, nearest first, as labels.

label.description:
Its filter, as the flats name it, and measured angle range: "Ha at
72.6° & 82.2°".

lightAngle.description:
The light's recorded angle, and how far the rotator's epochs turn
it into the family's nearest session.

lightRotation.description:
How the stacker's gate reads the light's angle: as recorded, or as
the angle of the flats its master is built from when measurement
gave it flats at another angle (seiza-calibration's
`LightRotation`).

pointed.description:
The family its lights pointed to, when that move was not confirmed
(`disputed`).

sampleLights.description: IDs refer to FlatLightContext, defaulting to the library light's index.

FlatGroupPlan.description:
A flat group plan: the book a request's rows make, and where each of its
lights stands. Indices refer to this plan's arrays, never to host
database rows. Keyed outputs are sorted lists of pairs, so their wire
format is stable.

pedestalAdu.description:
Optional cached host pedestal. None uses the library's bias level at
the light's gain and offset.

FlatRecord.description:
A flat's measurement, with the light cone its header recorded so its
session's dust, found later on the stack, can be placed too. Stored as
the measurement's own fields plus `optics`.

algorithmVersion.description:
[`FLAT_QUALITY_ALGORITHM_VERSION`] when this was measured; 1 when
stored without one.

channelLevels.description:
Median of each channel: one entry for mono, three for RGB, and four
for a CFA frame, one per site of the 2x2 pattern in the order top
left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.

clippedFraction.description: Share of finite samples within 0.1% of full scale.

detectionDepth.description:
How deep a dip had to be to count as a feature in this frame: the
larger of the configured depth and the configured multiple of the
smoothed noise.

featureCount.description: Features found, including any beyond the kept list.

features.description:
Large features (disks, donuts, patches) first, deepest first, then
compact and irregular dips, deepest first; at most 100,000.

fullScale.description: The full-scale value the frame was measured against.

noise.description:
Pixel-scale noise of the response, as a fraction of it. A CFA frame
is measured on its 2x2 sums.

vignetting.description:
Shadows hanging from the border that are not the image circle's own
fall-off: an off-axis guider's prism, a filter holder.

unplanned.description: Eligible raw flats without a capture time cannot establish night/change evidence.

FlatRetryAction.description: What a flat master does next.

oneOf.description: Publish the first build: it is stable, or nothing replaces it.

Build again from [`FlatRetryDecision::inputs`], the first set less
the frames that drift.
Publish the trimmed build.
Build the next flat session, [`FlatRetryDecision::inputs`].
Publish the next session's build.

Publish no flat master: the set is unstable and the policy keeps
none such.

inputs.description: The frames to build, by UUID, for a `Try` action; empty otherwise.

note.description: What the master's card says about the choice.

rebuildFirst.description:
The first build is a memo: should it serve, build it again for real
first.

FlatRetryPolicy.description:
Which retries a flat master may take when its frames disagree about
spots that come and go. The default is PSF Guard's: leave a minority
out, else take the next session, else keep the set and say so.

enabled.description: Judge a flat set at all; off, the first build always serves.

retainUnstable.description:
Keep an unstable set nothing replaces, with a note, rather than
withhold the flat.

trimUnstable.description: Rebuild without a minority of frames that disagree.

tryNextSession.description: Take the next flat session when the set as a whole disagrees.

session.description:
Pass the returned session directly to retain its policy, held-back rows
and resolved time window. Conflicting explicit overrides are rejected.

trimmedAttempted.description:
Set true when the retry failed/yielded no master. Successful feedback
implies attempted, so callers need not duplicate that state.

FlatSetStability.description:
How the frames of one flat set agree about the features their master
kept. A feature every frame shows the same way is a real property of the
optical path (a dust shadow, a dead cluster) and corrects the lights. A
feature the frames disagree about was changing while they were shot, and
the master's copy of it corrects nothing.

disagreement.description:
Per input frame, in `frames` order. Unreadable/incompatible inputs
reach the drift threshold; deliberately skipped inputs are zero.

driftThreshold.description:
Disagreeing pixels at or above which a frame counts as drifting: a
share of the sensor rather than of the features, so a dusty optical
path with many honest features cannot hide a droplet run.

errors.description: Input index and diagnostic for unreadable or incompatible sources.

featurePixels.description: Master pixels that depart from the smooth response around them.

FlatStabilityBayer.description: CFA pattern and phase for cached mono images. Offsets are zero or one.

FlatStabilityFileRequest.description: File form of the loaded-master measurement, shared by C and Python.

FlatStabilityImageMetadata.description:
Metadata for a cached source image. Pixels must already use the same units
as the master and optional bias/dark; no file headers or rescaling are used.

FlatStabilityImageOptions.description: Options shared by the C buffer and Python NumPy measurement entry points.

bayer.description: Default CFA layout for the master, sources and dark. A source may override it.

inputs.description: Empty uses default metadata for every source; otherwise aligned to inputs.

FlatUse.description: How a session's flat master applies to its lights.

oneOf.description: No flat master serves.
After a bias or dark master removed the pedestal.

With neither master: a pedestal must be fitted from sample lights
first ([`Application::sample_lights`]).
After subtracting the pedestal fitted from the lights.

With neither master nor a pedestal, because the host forced it:
vignetted edges may brighten.
Not at all: no reliable pedestal could be fitted.

grouping.description:
Feed evidence answers back into this resolved request. All manual rows
and catalog imaging sessions are preserved.

FlatWorkReview.description: Evidence and corrections, with the exact native rows used for selection.

algorithmVersion.description: Version of the native planning records.

corrections.description: Corrections that must be applied before stacking.

groupEdges.description: Native edge rows a host can offer to split/join.

grouping.description: The measured native grouping used for this review.

Frame.description: The native quality decision shown for one calibration file.

fingerprint.description: Metadata identity captured when this file was inspected.

grade.description: Native grade, absent for unmeasured/external records.

isMaster.description: Whether metadata identifies an existing external master.

kind.description: Calibration frame kind identified from its metadata.

measurementState.description: Whether the cached measurement is current, stale, missing, failed or external.

Grade.description: How a frame came out of screening, from best to worst.

oneOf.description: Nothing crossed a limit.
Something crossed the first limit: worth a look before use.
Something crossed the second limit: likely to harm a master.

Group.description: Where the panel shows a setting.

GroupChoice.description: What a person did to one edge between groups.

oneOf.description: A new group starts at the session.
The session's group and the one before it are one.

GroupEdge.description: A native edge on which a host can offer split/join commands.

row.description: The unchanged native command row, resolved by Seiza.

GroupNote.description: A group of one family, as a light's account names it.

GroupOption.description: A native measured group a personal choice can name.

frame.description: A flat frame anchoring this native group.

sessionKey.description: Native session identity anchoring this choice.

GroupOverrideRow.description: One split or join as the catalog keeps it.

anchorFrame.description: The first flat of the session that starts the later side: the edge.

beforeFrame.description: For a join, the session on the earlier side.

choice.description:
`None` once reset: kept, with when, so a copy's older choice does
not come back.

familyKey.description: The family's key when the choice was made.

label.description: The edge in words when it was made: "R at 104.0°, 2026-08-11 | 2026-08-12".

night.description:
The nights of the session the edge comes before, and of a join's
earlier session: they find the session again when its first flat is
kept out or forgotten, which renames it.

rotation.description:
The rotator angles those sessions record, beside their nights: the
night alone could name another angle's session of the family key.

GroupingReview.description: Measured native grouping visible to file-based hosts.

algorithmVersion.description: Version of the native planning records.

boundaries.description: Measured or manually chosen response boundaries.

events.description: Optical changes resolved by the native grouping book.

imaging.description: Imaging sessions formed from acquisition identities and times.

sessions.description: Unique master sessions or measured flat sessions.

HandEdge.description: How a person's choice changed an edge between groups.

IlluminationProfile.description:
A coarse map of how light falls across a flat: vignetting, gradients, and
broad shadows.

response.description:
Row-major median of each cell, divided by the median cell so a typical
cell reads 1. A cell with no finite samples reads 0.

ImagingSession.description: A continuous run of lights of one profile.

rigs.description: The rigs its profile shot with: only their lights it can place.

IncompleteLights.description: How preparation treats lights with missing, ungraded or undecided calibration.

oneOf.description: Refuse preparation until the host reviews incomplete lights.
Prepare the available calibration and retain incomplete lights.
Mark incomplete lights for the host to omit from its original input list.

Judged.description: A frame's grade against its peers, as [`grade`] judges it.

code.description: The finding that decided the grade.

strayLight.description: The stray-light mark, for a dark that caught light.

LibraryKinds.description:
Which kinds of usable frame the library holds for one light's sensor,
whatever their optics, exposure, age or validity mark. A light only
lacks what its library could have given it.

unusedDark.description:
Darks for this sensor that the light's rig does without
([`Rules::use_darks`]): the library still holds something for it.

Light.description: A light as matching reads it: its file and header.

rigUuid.description: The library rig it was shot with, by the key rigs are filed under.

rotatorPosition.description: Rotator angle in degrees at capture.

LightRotation.description:
How a light's rotator angle takes part in matching it to flats.

A recorded angle is the rotator's own reading. It is usually right, and
it is what [`MatchTolerances::rotation_deg`] compares by default. It can
also be wrong for the question a flat asks: a rotator re-homed or a
camera re-seated reads the same angle for a different position, and two
angles far apart can describe one light path when nothing ahead of the
rotator casts a shadow that turns. A host that measured which flats a
light's pixels follow — by plate solving it, or by fitting its sky
background against each candidate flat set — passes what it measured
here, so the stacker's gate follows that measurement rather than
refusing the flats it chose on the light's recorded angle.

Serialized as `{"basis": "recorded"}`, `{"basis": "measured",
"degrees": 82.2}` or `{"basis": "unknown"}`.

oneOf.description: The angle the light recorded, as for any frame.

An angle the host measured for the light, in degrees, compared in
place of the one it recorded: the light's flats must lie within
[`MatchTolerances::rotation_deg`] of it.

The host has measured that the angle does not decide this light's
flats: it is compared at no angle, as a light from a rig without a
rotator is ([`rotation_matches`]), and any flat angle passes.

MatchTolerances.description:
How close two readings have to be to count as the same.

The defaults are the ones a rig's own scatter needs rather than what a
specification promises: sensors report temperature to about a degree, and
a set-point hunts by more than that over a night.

Deliberately *not* `#[non_exhaustive]`, unlike [`FrameSignature`]. A new
tolerance changes what matches, so a consumer being made to look at it when
one is added is the point, not a cost — and it keeps
`MatchTolerances { rotation_deg: 0.5, ..Default::default() }` working,
which is how a config struct wants to be written.

Deserializing fills a missing field with its default, so tolerances saved
before a field was added still load. An unknown field is ignored, as for
any serde struct: these are a host's settings, and a newer file should
still open in an older host. A store where ignoring a newer gate would
match under the wrong one — seiza-stacking's saved context is one — keeps
its own type that refuses unknown fields.

Nothing stops a struct literal holding a value no comparison can use; see
[`Self::validate`] for the API that refuses them.

allowFlatGainOffsetMismatch.description:
Allow different gain/offset when selecting flats for lights and when
applying a master flat that records dark subtraction. The caller must
establish that the camera's normalized response is transferable across
these settings. Dark/light and flat/dark-flat matching remain strict.

darkTemperatureC.description: Dark sensor temperature against light sensor temperature, in Celsius.

exposureFraction.description:
Dark exposure against light exposure: the proportional part, as a
fraction of the longer of the two. Timing error scales with exposure,
so past about a minute this is what decides.

exposureSeconds.description:
Dark exposure against light exposure: the floor, in seconds.

The comparison takes whichever of this and
[`Self::exposure_fraction`] is larger, because neither works alone. A
fixed 0.05 s is a tenth of a half-second flat and a six-thousandth of a
five-minute sub — far too loose at one end and tighter than a shutter
can be trusted at the other.

flatSessionSeconds.description:
How far apart flats in one master may have been shot, in seconds.
Flats are a session's dust and vignetting; a week-old flat describes a
different optical train even when every setting agrees.

focalLengthMm.description: Focal length between a flat and what it corrects, in millimetres.

lightRotation.description:
How the light's own rotator angle is read when a flat is matched to
it: as recorded (the default), as the host measured it, or not at
all. Only the light's side of a light-against-flat question reads
it ([`optics_match`], [`describe_optics_mismatch`], and the
stacker's gate); flats judged against each other keep their
recorded angles. Not written when it is the default, so tolerances
saved before it existed read and write the same.

masterTemperatureC.description:
Sensor temperature within one master's input set, in Celsius. Tighter

this decides what may be averaged together.

rotationDeg.description:
Rotator angle between a flat and what it corrects, in degrees.

Wide enough to absorb a rotator re-homing to the same arrangement on
another night: a real rig re-slewed to nominally identical framing
with up to about 0.8 degrees of scatter, and a 1 degree gate split
those nights into separate flat sessions for no optical reason. Two
degrees still refuses a genuinely different framing, which sits tens
of degrees away, not fractions of one.
